primary.title: Orbits and resonances of the regular moons of Neptune
primary.status: Record reports accepted in Icarus 2019-10-01; final publisher article not downloaded in this audit.
primary.assessed: Sections 2–5 and Tables 1,2,5–7; full40page PDF retained, no figure embedded.

fit.observations: System data span1981–2016; Thalassa Table1 has45 Voyager sample/line pairs in1989, Table2 includes2002 Mauna Kea and HST2004,2005,2009,2016. Not a new native-image product crosswalk.
fit.model: nep090 weighted integrated orbital fit, Neptune-system barycentric ICRF, Neptune J2/J4, Triton, Sun and planets; fixed pole, DE435/NEP081 and Voyager camera bias.
fit.GM_limit: Formal post-fit1sigma without mass prior for Thalassa; subtle residual improvement/borderline data sensitivity. Removing Voyager increases Naiad/Thalassa mass errors >60%; halving Voyager weight shifts Thalassa mass ~.03sigma versus Naiad ~.5sigma. Other moon prior-constrained masses are not equivalent measurements.
fit.radius_source: Table5 adopts Karkoschka2003 Voyager imaging size; no new fitted axes, pixel measurement or catalogue update.
fit.density_limit: Derived from fitted GM and adopted radius, propagating both errors; not measured local composition, porosity or material fractions. Table5 theoretical .05–1.5g/cm3 prior range is not measured density.

Table7_Thalassa.reference: Individual local Laplace plane, not scene camera/equator

fit.mean_element_limit: 900-year integration summarized by precessing ellipses. Authors assign no mean-element uncertainties: ellipse-fit errors would not represent observational uncertainty. Not dated current distance, perfect circle, surface normal or spin period.

resonance.type: Fourth-order inclination resonance involving Naiad node; not spin resonance.
resonance.mass_sensitivity: Changing Thalassa GM to 0.03 km3/s2 (+1 sigma) gives about46deg/1.7yr; not universal fixed constants.
resonance.conjunction: Simplified integrated geometry south,south,north,north offsets; historical lower-order captures and Triton-related origins remain interpretations.
